correctness.rationale: With leaves parametrized by their intersection with the vertical transversal, the source's Lipschitz-foliation inequality makes the vertical gap between any two nearby lifted leaves uniformly comparable to the parameter gap. Integrating that gap gives the Lebesgue area of the strip, hence the leaf-space marginal measure of the corresponding arc. Area preservation and leaf equivariance make this marginal invariant. Its cumulative distribution lift is bi-Lipschitz and, by invariance, conjugates the induced leaf homeomorphism to a rigid rotation; rotation-number invariance identifies that rotation with the source's irrational angle. Theorem C then gives minimality. Boundary leaves have zero area, wrap-around arcs are handled by periodic lifts, and no finite experiment is used.

originality.rationale: The motivating preprint retains bi-Lipschitz regularity of the conjugacy as a separate hypothesis and explicitly distinguishes it from the bi-Lipschitz regularity of the induced leaf map. Targeted statement-level searches and own-ledger checks found no equivalent removal of that hypothesis. The closest older twist-map integrability theorem concerns a different regime in which every annulus leaf is individually invariant and therefore does not imply the present leaf-space result.
residual_risks: The focal preprint is very recent, and a later revision may add this observation.

The theorem does not remove the transverse Lipschitz-foliation assumption, so literature proving that stronger regularity automatically in this exact setting would strictly dominate it; no such result was found.

value.rationale: The focal paper identifies bi-Lipschitz regularity of the leaf-space conjugacy as a main extra ingredient in its minimality theorem. The new argument shows that area preservation plus transverse Lipschitz geometry already forces that regularity, deleting the separate conjugacy hypothesis. This sharpens the theorem and isolates the remaining obstruction to the broader minimality problem: whether the invariant foliation produced by the source has transverse Lipschitz regularity.
